newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK YIELD CURVE, DRACHMA UP ON CENBANK MOVE.
newsitem.headline: GREEK YIELD CURVE, DRACHMA UP ON CENBANK MOVE.

text.p: The Greek yield curve firmed across-the-board with the rise more accentuated in short tenors strengthening the drachma against the ecu after the central bank surprised the market by draining a larger-than-expected amount of 14-day funds, traders said.

The central bank surprised the market by draining 250 billion drachmas of 14-day funds at 11.90 percent in its regular Wednesday tender. A pact of 200 billion drachmas was maturing today so that a net amount of 50 billion drachmas left the system.
Bonds were little affected with wider price spreads as offers held but bids receded.
"Depos jumped across-the-board on the central bank's surprise move," said a dealer at a private bank. "The rise was more accentuated in short tenors but rates have come off lows in late dealings."
Dealers said the central bank opted to defend the drachma by raising interest rates and hopefully prompt sales of ecus that would boost interbank liquidity and contain the rate rise.
The drachma was trading below 310 against the ecu in late dealings on moderate ecu selling for drachmas in response to higher interest rates.
The mark was quoted at 158.79/84 from Wednesday's 158.980 fix, the dollar at 274.70/80 drachmas from 275.320 and the ecu at 309.82/92 from 310.450 drachmas.
